title: Brain Tumor MRI Benchmark Audit: patient-identifier recovery, leakage analysis, and a patient-disjoint split
description:
Audit tooling and corrected evaluation splits for a widely used four-class brain tumor MRI benchmark (7,023 images; Mendeley/Kaggle mirror of a figshare-derived collection).

This deposit contains:

  • figshare_patient_map.json — a recovered figshare patient identifier for 4,586 of the 5,023 tumor images, obtained by crop-normalized, orientation-invariant content matching against the source collection. The aggregated release discards patient identity, which is why the leakage it contains had not previously been measurable.
  • cv_folds.json — a fixed five-fold patient-disjoint partition in which every patient is assigned to exactly one test fold, plus near-duplicate cluster grouping for the no-tumor class, which has no recoverable patient structure.
  • Audit tooling — duplicate and near-duplicate detection, provenance matching with a calibrated sensitivity control, redundancy counting, and split construction.
  • Pipeline — training, evaluation, calibration and interpretability code, with pinned dependency versions and per-run metrics.

Key findings: 206 of 233 patients appear in both released folders; every traceable tumor test image belongs to a patient also present in training; 216 test images (16.5%) are pixel-identical to a training image; and the 7,023 files contain only 6,597 distinct images. Under patient-disjoint cross-validation, accuracy falls from 99.22% to 95.19% (93.68% on tumor classes alone).

Only derived metadata is redistributed here. The underlying images are third-party and must be obtained from their original sources.
